items_list.fact: Three reasons for little adoption: complexity (top-k, multiple aux losses, capacity juggling), instability (bf16; GShard fell back to float32), communication cost

items_list.fact: Take T5, replace the FFN in every other block with a Switch layer: N expert FFNs plus a linear router W_r

checks: replace the feed-forward network (FFN) in every other Transformer block
expert FFNs plus a linear router

items_list.fact: Router logits h(x) = W_r x, softmax to p_i(x), send to the argmax expert
items_list.where: The paper tab, Idea; animation
checks: softmax turns them into gate values
the token goes to the single expert with the largest one

items_list.fact: Output = chosen expert output scaled by gate value p_i(x), keeps router differentiable

items_list.fact: Aux loss per Switch layer: f_i fraction dispatched (argmax, non-differentiable), P_i mean router probability (differentiable), loss = alpha N sum f_i P_i
items_list.where: The paper tab, Balancing loss
checks: an argmax count with no gradient

items_list.fact: Minimised by uniform routing at 1/N; N factor keeps magnitude constant across expert counts; alpha = 1e-2 balances without disturbing LM loss
items_list.where: The paper tab, Balancing loss
checks: is minimized under a uniform distribution
keeps it constant as the expert count changes
small enough not to interfere with the cross-entropy objective

items_list.fact: This single loss replaces the separate load and importance losses of Shazeer 2017
items_list.where: The paper tab, Balancing loss

items_list.fact: Pure bfloat16 diverges (router softmax and exponentials); pure float32 stable but float32 all-to-all (1160 vs 1390 examples/s)

items_list.fact: Fix: cast to float32 only inside the router, locally; recast dispatch and combine tensors to bf16 before communication; float32 stability at bf16 speed
items_list.where: The paper tab, Precision

recast the dispatch and combine tensors to bfloat16
